title: Gold demand down 30% in September quarter as high prices hurt jewellery sales - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Gold demand in the September quarter plunged 30 per cent to 162 tonnes against 230 tonnes. | Photo Credit: RUPAK DE CHOWDHURI

Gold demand in India during the September quarter plunged 30 per cent to 162 tonnes against 230 tonnes logged in the same period last year as the high prices pulled down jewellery sales.

In value terms, the gold demand was up 3 per cent at ₹2.42 lakh crore (₹2.35 lakh crore), largely due to rupee depreciation against dollar, according to the World Gold Council data released on Tuesday.

Jewellery demand declined 20 per cent to 100 tonne (125 tonne) with consumers holding back their purchases due to high prices. Jewellery demand in value terms was up 16 per cent to ₹1.49 lakh crore (₹1.28 lakh crore).

Sachin Jain, Regional CEO, India, World Gold Council said as gold prices increased, consumers prioritised the purchases while adapting to balance affordability with long-term value.

However, jewellery demand revived by a pullback in gold prices late in Q3, which encouraged some deferred purchases, he said.

While official bullion imports fell sharply and recycling remained muted, he said preliminary estimates point to increased unofficial inflows. With the rise in import duty, illegal gold imports hit a 3-Year high in the September quarter. Illegal gold imports rose to 50 tonnes in Q3 2026, compared to just 3 tonnes in Q3 2025, according to the WGC report.

Gold bars and coins demand plunged 40 per cent to 55 tonne (92 tonne) as the import duty was doubled to 15 per cent. In value terms, it down 13 per cent to ₹81,890 crore (₹93,740 crore).

Net gold imports were down 46 per cent to 114 tonne (212 tonne) in the quarter under review. Recycled gold also dropped 12 per cent to 19 tonne (22 tonne).

The average gold prices spiked 23 per cent to $4,262 an ounce ($3,457 an ounce). In India, it jumped 46 per cent to ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams against ₹1.02 lakh in the same period last year.

Gold ETF (exchange traded fund) demand halved to 5.3 tonne (10.7 tonne) and its value declined to 28 per cent to ₹7,890 crore (₹10,940 crore). Digital gold purchases was down 44 per cent at 4.9 tonne (3.4 tonne).

RBI restrained buying gold in the Q3 against 0.2 tonne bought in the September quarter last year.

The softening of gold prices will revive demand in the December quarter, particularly during the festival season starting with Dhanteras and longer wedding season, said Jain.

The investment demand is also reviving going by the inflows in gold ETFs towards the end of the quarter, which reached a seven-month high in September, he added.
